latest.title: H1-26 Trading Update
latest.content:
Today 07:00
RNS Number : 0550O
Creo Medical Group PLC
28 July 2026
Creo Medical Group plc
("Creo", the "Company" or the "Group")
H1-26 Trading Update
45% increase in H1-26 revenues
Continued commercial momentum and a materially lower cost base
Confident in delivering full year performance in line with management expectations
Creo Medical Group plc (AIM: CREO), the medical device company focused on the emerging field of minimally invasive surgical endoscopy for pre-cancer and cancer patients, provides a trading update for the six months ended 30 June 2026 ("H1-26").
Financial highlights
The Group has continued to make strong operational and strategic progress through the second quarter of this financial year. Revenue for H1-26 increased by 45% to £3.2m (H1-25: £2.2m). Trading for the period was in line with management expectations, supporting the Board's confidence in delivering full year revenue growth in line with existing guidance of 50% to 60%. This full year guidance is underpinned by a strong order book carried into Q3-26, the Group's usual H2-weighted revenue profile and continued expansion into new regions, particularly in LATAM.
Management has remained focused on scaling the commercial platform, reducing the Group's operating cost base and simplifying the business. Underlying operating costs for H1-26 decreased by 15% to £7.8m (H1-25: £9.1m). The disposal and outsourcing of the Company's manufacturing operations, announced on 16 April 2026, completed during the second quarter and further supports the Group's path towards profitability and a more scalable operating model. Underlying operating loss on a continuing basis reduced by over 25% in H1-26 to £4.9m (H1-25: £6.9m).
In May 2026, Creo announced the proposed sale of its remaining 49% interest in Creo Medical SL ("CME Stake Disposal") and completed an equity placing raising approximately £5.5 million, alongside the establishment of a £2.0 million convertible loan note instrument subscribed for by the Development Bank of Wales. Creo continues to progress the CME Stake Disposal, with completion expected during Q3-26. Together, the completed financing actions in H1-26 and anticipated proceeds from the CME Stake Disposal are expected to strengthen the Group's near-term funding position and provide additional strategic flexibility as the Group executes its H2 priorities. Cash and cash equivalents at 30 June 2026 were £7.4m (31 December 2025: £12.4m) and, subject to completion of the CME Stake Disposal, the Directors believe that the strengthened balance sheet will provide the Group with sufficient cash resources to fund its development through to sustainable cash flow generation and profitability.
Operational overview
Commercial and clinical momentum continued across the product portfolio during the period, supported by increased third-party clinical validation and procedural adoption. Key developments included the first UK private hospital use of Speedboat, key opinion leader presentations at DDW supporting Creo's core products, novel BEAM procedures using SpydrBlade™ Flex, and the milestone of 50 clinical cases using MicroBlate™ Fine.
Earlier this month, the Company announced that MicroBlate™ Flex had exceeded 100 clinical cases, reflecting increasing utilisation, growing clinician engagement and accelerating adoption across leading centres.
Outlook
The Board remains encouraged by trading into the second half of 2026, supported by a strong order book carried into Q3-26, the Group's usual H2-weighted revenue profile and the continued growth in clinical and commercial validation. Together with the benefits of a lower cost base, the Board remains confident in delivering full year revenue growth in line with existing guidance of 50% to 60%.
Notice of Interim Results
Creo will announce its unaudited interim results for the six months ended 30 June 2026 in September 2026. A further announcement confirming the publication date of the interim results will be issued in due course.
Craig Gulliford, Chief Executive Officer of Creo, said:
"
We have delivered a strong first half, with the actions taken during the period strengthening the foundations of the Group. We have made further strategic progress, improved our operating platform and established a materially lower cost base. With growing clinical and commercial momentum across the portfolio, we remain well placed for the second half and confident in delivering our full year guidance.

latest.title: MicroBlate™ Flex exceeds 100 clinical cases
latest.content:
23 Jul 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 4630N
Creo Medical Group PLC
23 July 2026
Creo Medical Group plc
("Creo", the "Company" or the "Group")
MicroBlate™ Flex exceeds 100 clinical cases as adoption builds
Milestone
reflects increasing
utilisation
across leading centres in the UK and Europe
and the potential long-term commercial opportunity for Creo's flexible microwave ablation product
Creo Medical Group plc (AIM: CREO), the medical device company focused on the emerging field of minimally invasive surgical endoscopy for pre-cancer and cancer patients, announces that more than 100 clinical cases have now been completed using its MicroBlate™ Flex microwave ablation product.
Exceeding 100 clinical cases marks an important step in building procedural expertise and clinical confidence. This milestone reflects the continuing progress in the clinical rollout of MicroBlate™ Flex following the previously announced commencement of lung tumour procedures. It also indicates increased use of a new breakthrough device changing lung cancer treatment as clinicians gain experience with the product and its integration into emerging minimally invasive treatment pathways. While the product is still at an early stage of roll-out the Company expects case numbers to rise rapidly over the next 12 months.
MicroBlate™ Flex is Creo's soft tissue microwave ablation product, designed to deliver precise, controlled ablation of nodules and tumours in several tissue types through a flexible endoscopic platform. MicroBlate™ Flex is particularly suited to the treatment of hard-to-reach lesions, including lung tumours, where minimally invasive access and precise energy delivery are critical. Management believe the potential market size for MicroBlate™ Flex applications is significant.
Alongside commercial development, Creo remains focused on expanding the clinical evidence base for MicroBlate™ Flex through ongoing clinical studies, post-market data generation, investigator-led research and scientific publications. Importantly, the growing body of clinical experience is contributing to the continued development of treatment workflows combining robotic-assisted navigation and flexible microwave ablation. This forms part of Creo's previously announced long-term collaboration with Intuitive Surgical, Inc. and is helping to build real-world experience in minimally invasive robotic-assisted lung tumour treatment pathways.
Commenting on the clinical experience, Professor Pallav Shar, Consultant Respiratory Physician, Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust, said:
"The utility of robotic assisted bronchoscopy with Creo's MicroBlate™ Flex microwave ablation system broadens treatment options, particularly for patients with severe lung disease who may not have any other treatment options."
Commenting on the milestone, Craig Gulliford, Chief Executive Officer of Creo Medical, said:
"This milestone is a clear signal that the adoption and utilisation of MicroBlate™ Flex is building. We are seeing growing clinician engagement and utilisation, encouraging integration into clinical workflows across participating centres and real-world momentum as physicians gain experience with the product and its capabilities.
"The procedures in which MicroBlate™ Flex is being used have additional strategic value in helping clinicians develop treatment pathways that combine robotic navigation and microwave ablation, while also contributing to the evidence, workflow development and understanding of health economics that will support broader adoption.
"Together with our ongoing post-market clinical programme and previously announced long-term collaboration with Intuitive, this milestone is another important step in establishing MicroBlate™ Flex as a differentiated product in the evolving treatment landscape for early-stage lung cancer, where increasing rates of earlier diagnosis are creating greater demand for precise, minimally invasive options."

Creo Medical Group PLC

Creo Medical Group plc
("Creo" the "Company" or the "Group")
Award of Shares under Share Incentive Plan and Director Dealings
Creo Medical Group plc (AIM: CREO),
the medical device company focused on the emerging field of minimally invasive surgical endoscopy for pre-cancer and cancer patients
, implemented an HMRC approved Share Incentive Plan ("SIP") during 2020, which is available to all of the Company's UK based employees, including Directors.
The Company has been notified that Fiduchi Trustees (UK) Limited ("Fiduchi"), the independent trustee of the SIP, acquired, in accordance with the SIP's rules and on behalf of SIP participants, 143,541 ordinary shares in the Company ("Ordinary Shares"), at a price of £0.144 per Ordinary Share on 1 July 2026 to meet its obligations under the SIP (the "Partnership Shares"). Under the terms of the SIP, the Company is required to issue or make available to the SIP, to be allocated to participants, two Ordinary Shares in the Company for each Partnership Share purchased (being 287,082 Ordinary Shares, the "Matching Shares"). As at 1 July 2026, Fiduchi held 875,247 unallocated Ordinary Shares within the SIP. 287,082 of these unallocated Ordinary Shares will be utilised to meet the SIP Matching Share obligation and, accordingly, no new Ordinary Shares are required to be issued to satisfy the Company's obligations under the SIP.
Craig Gulliford and Richard Rees, executive directors of the Company (the "Participating Directors"), have acquired Partnership Shares at a price of £0.144 per share at Fiduchi's sole discretion and received Matching Shares at a price of £0.001 per share in accordance with terms of the SIP (the "Transaction"). About Creo Medical
Creo is a medical device company focused on the development and commercialisation of minimally invasive electrosurgical devices, bringing advanced energy to endoscopy.
The Company's vision is to improve patient outcomes through the development and commercialisation of a suite of electrosurgical medical devices, each enabled by CROMA, powered by Kamaptive. The Group has developed the CROMA powered by Kamaptive full-spectrum adaptive technology to optimise surgical capability and patient outcomes. Kamaptive is a seamless, intuitive integration of multi-modal energy sources, optimised to dynamically adapt to patient tissue during procedures such as resection, dissection, coagulation, and ablation of tissue. Kamaptive technology provides clinicians with increased flexibility, precision and controlled surgical solutions. CROMA currently delivers bipolar radiofrequency ("RF") energy for precise localised cutting and focused high frequency microwave ("MW") energy for controlled coagulation and ablation via a single accessory port. This technology, combined with the Group's range of patented electrosurgical devices, is designed to provide clinicians with flexible, accurate and controlled clinical solutions. The Directors believe the Company's technology can impact the landscape of surgery and endoscopy by providing a safer, less invasive and more cost-efficient option for procedures.

company_30s.what_they_do: CREO specialises in miniature surgical instruments – tiny lasers (MicroBlate) and cutting blades (SpydrBlade) that are used in endoscopic and minimally‑invasive procedures.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The market for small‑bore, precision tools is growing as surgeons move away from open surgery. CREO’s products are designed to be cheaper, easier to use and safer, giving the company a potential first‑mover edge in oncology, ENT and urology.
company_30s.current_state: The firm is in a pivot phase: it has sold a 49 % stake in its Spanish subsidiary, raised capital, and is pushing product approvals. Revenues are modest and cash burn remains high, but the company is actively courting hospitals and key opinion leaders.

rns_narrative: Product progress: MicroBlate has cleared 100 clinical cases and SpydrBlade is in use for novel beam procedures – signalling tangible market traction.
Capital manoeuvres: a £5.5 m placing and the sale of a subsidiary stake are aimed at extending runway and funding further development.
Governance updates: AGM, appointment of a corporate broker and share‑incentive awards show the board is keeping the company compliant while motivating insiders.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet skepticism – most chatter is about cash burn and unclear product traction, with a handful of hopeful voices.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: A few traders point to the recent clinical milestones as evidence that the company could finally break out.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Many observers warn that the firm has not yet proven commercial viability and could run out of money before it turns profitable.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The tone has stayed flat; a few new posts about clinical success have not yet sparked broader optimism.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for CREO is flat – no recent search spikes, which is a sign of maximum surprise potential.

near_term_catalysts: Regulatory approval or a positive KOL endorsement for MicroBlate or SpydrBlade that could drive hospital adoption.
Completion of the £5.5 m placing or the sale of the subsidiary stake, giving the company enough cash to fund commercialisation.
A significant volume spike at the 52‑week low that would confirm capitulation is over.
Positive earnings or cash‑flow update that shows a reduction in burn rate.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a 2× average daily volume, a break above the 50‑day moving average, and any mention of a new partnership or reimbursement decision in the next 60 days.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early stages of a potential recovery – the APEX compression score suggests a tight range, but mean‑reversion has not yet kicked in. A clear sign of capitulation is needed before a bounce is credible.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: If the company secures approvals and demonstrates real‑world adoption, the price could climb back to the middle of its 52‑week range – a 200 % upside from the current low. The deep crash (over 70 % from peak) gives the upside a favourable asymmetry.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: If the firm fails to raise capital, or if the products fail to gain traction, the stock may stay near its low or decline further. The worst‑case is a continued slide to zero if the business model cannot be monetised.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside 200–300 % versus a downside limited to the current price (effectively zero). The ratio is roughly 2 : 1 in favour of the upside, with the risk of a flat or slightly negative return if catalysts fail.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter after a bounce off the 52‑week low when volume exceeds 1.5× the 20‑day average. Size 10 % of the portfolio, stop 10 % below the low to protect against a false break.
playbook.if_watching: Hold until you see a volume spike and a break above the 50‑day MA, or until a regulatory/clinical announcement is made.
playbook.if_passing: If the company files for bankruptcy or is delisted, exit immediately; otherwise remain bullish on the deep‑crash set‑up.

ai_insights.bottom_line: CREO is a deeply discounted medical‑device maker on the brink of potential product adoption; a contrarian bet that capitalises on a 70‑plus % crash could pay off once a regulatory or partnership catalyst confirms mean‑reversion.
